title: Denver Breakfast Casserole
subtitle: Ham, bell peppers, and onion baked into a make-ahead egg strata.
description: Classic Denver omelette flavors in a 9x13 bake: diced ham, peppers, and onion folded through cubed bread and an egg-milk custard. Assembles the night before for an easy oven push on busy mornings.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Denver Breakfast Casserole in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Toast the bread cubes
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 350°F. Spread bread cubes on a sheet pan and toast 6–8 minutes until dry at the edges. Cool slightly so they don't turn the custard soggy. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the pan
steps.instruction: Butter a deep 9x13 dish. Layer half the bread, ham, peppers, onion, and half the cheese. Repeat layers, finishing with cheese on top. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Whisk the custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs with milk, dry mustard, salt, pepper, and a pinch of paprika until smooth. Pour evenly over the bread—press gently so cubes soak without compacting. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest or refrigerate
steps.instruction: Rest 30 minutes at room temperature, or cover and refrigerate overnight for a true make-ahead. Bring closer to room temp before baking if chilled. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Bake at 375°F until puffed, golden at the edges, and a knife inserted in the center comes out clean. Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares for the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Prep and refrigerate the casserole the night before a busy shift; pull it 30 minutes before baking.
Assign one cook to oven checks while another sets up a warm holding pan with foil for staggered eaters.
Cut with a sharp serrated knife in the pan, then lift squares with a offset spatula to keep layers intact.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 in warm soapy water immediately after serving—egg custard bonds to metal if left to dry.
Line the sheet pan with parchment when toasting bread cubes for a one-wipe cleanup.
leftovers: Wrap individual squares in foil and reheat at 325°F for 12 minutes until steaming in the center.
Dice cold casserole into a breakfast fried rice with soy, green onion, and a fried egg on top.
